recipes.name: Braised Oxtails in Red Wine Sauce
ingredients_raw: 5 pounds beef oxtail, cut into pieces

steps.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

Simmer the red wine in a large saucepan over medium-high heat until reduced by half. Meanwhile, combine the flour, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Dredge the oxtail in the seasoned flour, and shake off excess; set aside. Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a roasting pan over medium-high heat. Brown the oxtail on all sides, about 10 minutes.

Remove the oxtails from the pan and set aside. Turn the heat to medium-low and melt another 1 tablespoon of butter in the pan. Stir in the shallots, garlic, onion, carrots, and celery. Cook and stir until the vegetables have softened, about 10 minutes. Stir in the thyme, bay leaf, parsley, beef broth, and reduced red wine. Place the browned oxtail on top of the vegetables in a single layer, then bring to a boil.
Cover with a tight fitting lid or aluminum foil, then bake in preheated oven until the oxtail is very tender and nearly falling off the bone, 3 to 3 1/2 hours.

Once the oxtail is tender, remove the meat to a serving dish, cover, and keep warm. Strain the remaining braising liquid through a mesh strainer into a saucepan. Simmer over medium-high heat until the sauce has reduced to 2 cups. Whisk in the remaining 2 tablespoons butter and pour over the oxtail to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Braised Oxtails in Red Wine Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Oxtails are browned in butter before they go into the oven for a long slow roast that makes them perfectly tender. This is a perfect dish on a cold winter day.

review.reviewBody: A rich dish. I added 2 cups sliced small Bella mushrooms during the last hour. Spooned over a background of soft cooked grits. Oxtails are all about deep smooth flavor. I upped the garlic and onions, salt and pepper to give it some edges. The recipe works well for this classic. I might spoon in some tomato paste and up the liquid next time.

When I bought the oxtails (I'd never eaten nor cooked them before) my husband faked a gag and said his mom used to make vegetable soup with oxtails and that's why he hated vegetable soup until he'd met me. He said he'd trust me as I'm a great cook, but also asked me what we'd have as a "back up" in case oxtail was truly awful. Well!!! This was decadently fabulous! I pretty much followed the instructions as written. I took someone's suggestion of marinating the oxtails in the red wine (I used Bogle Old Vine Zin - only 1/2 a bottle) and added several cloves of sliced garlic. I marinated for about 4 hours. I then heavily dredged the tails in the seasoned flour and used a cast iron skillet to pan sautee them in a mixture of bacon grease and butter. Once the tails had a good crust on them I placed them on top of uncooked celery and carrots in a tall dutch oven. I then deglazed the cast iron skillet with the marinating liquid and garlic, gently stiring and letting it thicken/reduce to roughly 1/2. I then poured the contents of the skillet over the tails in the dutch oven. I then added the beef broth, pouring it directly over the contents of the dutch oven. Cooked for about 4 hours at 350. The dish was so rich and flavorful and the meat just fell off the bones. This is more than enough for at least 4 or 5 people. I served it with mashed garlic potatoes and sweet and sour German red cabbage on the side with sourdough toasts. WOW! Oh...and my husband said he'd never

I love this recipe...have never eaten oxtail before this. Wasn't even sure what they were, so I googled it and found it sounded too good to skip. Then I found this recipe...It reminded me of a recipe for Beef Bourguignon that I love. It is every bit as rich as that...but with a little more subtle overall flavor. 

I will make one change next time and that would be to soak the oxtail in the red wine overnight...that will help breakdown the toughness even more than just slow cooking alone. The only other change I made was I added more garlic powder...it was actually an accident...but one I liked. I served it over an al dente' fettuccine which was a perfect match for the sauce. Speaking of sauce...OMG! Yet another reminder that if you cook full flavored, rich food, you don't need typical American type portions. A much smaller portion was very satisfying. The only problem I had was that I got impatient and didn't reduce the wine enough in the first part of the recipe, which left me with too much liquid at the end so I had to reduce that more to make up for it. That's my own fault and a reminder to all to take your time and don't rush this one. You'll be glad you didn't because the final outcome is perfect if you follow this recipe.
Delicious and easy! I made it in my instant pot so that reduced my cooking time. Even my mom who doesn't like oxtails said they were delicious.

I've made this with a similar recipe . But, instead of thyme it called for oregano, I also used celery salt instead of celery root/stalk ,1 bottle of red wine , 1 cup of broth, no flour . But I suppose that is to thicken the fluid. It also called to season the oxtail with allspice , salt , and pepper over night or at least 2 hours marinating . Seared the oxtails before putting it in the liquid mixture. Placed everything in a Dutch oven & covered . My oxtails were cut so thick so I cooked it for 2 1/2 hours on 325 in the oven. Tastes heavenly. This is how I'm going to make it all the time .

This was amazing. I basically followed the recipe but added mushrooms, potatoes, extra carrots, and peas toward the end. I cooked it in my le creuset pot for over 3 1/2 hours and the meat was falling off the bone. Rave reviews from my friends. Fantastic flavor. Will definitely make again.
So good as it is but next time I think I'll take the top off the pot an hour be free taking it out of the oven. I also will add some button mushrooms with the carrots and onions.

Love this recipe! I substituted beef shanks for the oxtails... they were more readily available and a lot cheaper. Not to mention was just as tender and delicious with a ton more (accessible)meat. The shanks actually turned out better for me than my oxtails did.

I made this recipe just as it was written except I didn’t have shallots and I used onions. The red wine sauce was really good but a little bit strong for me. I will make this again but next time I’ll cut it with a little bit more beef broth so it has more beef flavor than wine flavor. That was the first time of ever had ox tails and they were super tender and way more meaty then I ever thought. This dish went really well with rice and gremolotta.

Very delicious! I served it over rice. I did add a wee bit more garlic but other than that I didnt change a thing. I did however cook it as directed but in a crockpot at low for 3 hrs. Still turned out fine! thanks for a great recipe.

OMG! This was AMAZING! I followed the recipe almost and it turned out perfect. The only thing I did differently was to salt the actual oxtail pieces rather than mix the salt in with the flour and garlic/onion powder. Also, I didn't have onion powder so I just used double garlic powder and it was still awesome. This is definitely going to be my go-to meal if I need to impress someone! Cook it the full time...I did only 2.5 hours and it was not fall-off-the-bone which meant it was harder to eat.
Prefect cheat day dish! Easy and full of sin.
delicious on rice. the whole family loved it and I froze the extra sauce for roast.
This is my all time favorite recipe. I am asked repeatedly to make it for my family and friends. I follow the recipe exactly and they turn out perfect, savory, delicious every time.
This was a different option for my husband's change in diet. I cut out most of the salt, using a low salt or no salt seasoning. He was delighted and asked for me to make it again.
Wow 5 star dish for sure!! I added mushrooms and served it over Gnocchi, YUMMY!! Thank you for this great recipe
Delicious and an easy recipe to follow for my first time ever cooking oxtails. Thank you so much, I will make this again and again.
just a delicious dinner
So delicious! 10/10 will make again another another cold weekend day. Tender and succulent.
I increased the butter, garlic powder, and onion powder and added fresh tarragon, sliced white mushrooms, and french green beans. Very rich and delicious. My wife was impressed!
